title: Glessner's stable roof brought down to the old pictures
items: The roof over the Glessner stable's alley end is lower: its ridge sits about two feet lower and two feet further north, on the same pitch, so the slope carries the 42 or 43 rows of tiles that the 1887 print and the 1963 survey photograph both show, where it had about 51. The alley gable now stands up past the roof as a stone parapet with a coping, as both pictures draw it.
